findings.description: `publish()` saves `s.posted` as the full proof count before the description PATCH or any proof comment succeeds. If either GitHub operation fails, a later owner retry reaches the count-based return and never publishes the missing material.
findings.title: Failed posts leave PR proofs missing

evidence.explanation: The state save precedes both remote writes, while the early return trusts that saved count. GitHub CLI failures propagate through `write()` and `comment()`, and `continueRun()` invokes `publish()` again after a run is reopened.

findings.description: `publish()` treats a missing `s.posted` field as zero and selects every proof after the first as a new comment. Runs saved by the previous runner have no such field, so resuming one with existing proof comments posts those comments again.
findings.title: Old runs repost published proof comments

citations.citation: The earlier publication fix read PR state to avoid reposting proofs from older or interrupted runs.

evidence.explanation: The new default selects all proofs after index zero without reading comments. The existing publication tests explicitly cover an older run with its second proof already posted; the prior fix used PR content to exclude it.

findings.description: `publish()` returns on the saved count without checking whether the PR still contains the proofs it represents. If a proof is removed from the description or its comment is deleted while the run continues, later publication steps leave that proof absent.
findings.title: Removed PR proofs are not restored

citations.citation:
**7. The runner trusts what GitHub shows, not its own notes** (the Fresh Read Rule)
- **Rule:** the runner decides from what GitHub shows now, all of it: every page of comments, events and labels, read with `allPages`. What it saves between runs (counts, markers like `lastAsk` and `pushedAt`, local files like `<n>-pr-body.md`) is only a note. When a note and GitHub disagree, GitHub wins. Nothing is marked posted, read or done until GitHub shows it happened.
- **Where:** `scripts/agent-watch.mjs` and `scripts/runner-lib.mjs`: every read of tickets, PRs, comments, events and labels, and everything the runner saves about them. Rule 3 covers the same idea in `web/`.
- **Why:** this was the most common cause in Qodo's reviews of the runner: 8 of its 26 findings, across 4 PRs. I wrote the rule from #48, #51 and #53, then checked it against #60, which it hadn't seen. It predicted 3 of #60's 6 findings. The rest belong to other causes.
- **Breaks it:** reading only the first 100 comments or events (#48). Changing the local PR description and not the PR (#51). Moving `lastAsk` past an instruction that hasn't been carried out (#53). Saving a proof as posted when it was only rehearsed (#60).
- **Checked by:** `tests/runner-lib.test.mjs` (`allPages` reads past 100, `publishPlan` works out what to post from the PR itself, `askPlan` marks a comment read). In review: any GitHub read that stops at one page, any decision made from a saved note that GitHub could contradict and anything marked done before GitHub shows it.
… (1 more lines)

evidence.explanation: The old publication planner checks the PR body and comments for missing proofs; the new early return bypasses that check. The repository's Fresh Read Rule explicitly treats saved counts as notes that must yield to GitHub state.
